final_prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: wide cover infographic illustration for a Chinese technology blog article, aspect ratio 2.35:1. Primary request: create a clear conceptual cover explaining .NET garbage collection fundamentals. Theme: the garbage collector traces reachable objects from roots, reclaims unreachable space, and compacts suitable heap regions. Summary angle: one quiet archive curator manages a wide memory library; a single luminous reference thread reveals which storage boxes are still reachable, disconnected boxes are removed, and surviving boxes slide together to leave one continuous free space. Narrative flow: 3-beat process. Information blocks: first, the curator follows one luminous thread through reachable boxes with the approved label exactly '标记'; second, disconnected faded boxes leave the shelf with the approved label exactly '回收'; third, surviving boxes slide neatly together and reveal a clean continuous empty shelf with the approved label exactly '压缩'. Main metaphor: the managed heap as a calm archive library, references as borrowing threads, and GC as one careful curator. Primary subject: exactly one archive curator interacting with one luminous reference thread. Composition: ultra-wide left-to-right continuous scene, three connected beats without separate panels, curator and thread remain the dominant focus, ample negative space, simple readable shelf geometry, clear at thumbnail size. Style/medium: combine abstract technical concept art with low-saturation arthouse illustration, quiet composition, subtle grain, muted colors, reflective emotional tone. Use gray-blue, warm gray, muted teal-green, and small amber accents. Visible text policy: render only '标记', '回收', and '压缩'; no title, sentences, English words, formulas, numbers, extra labels, fake UI, watermark, or prompt residue. Constraints: exactly one curator, three supporting narrative beats, no product logos, no screenshots, no fake charts, no fake terminal output, no fabricated metrics, no unrelated icon collage. Avoid trash-can mascots, generic robots, code rain, neon city backgrounds, giant HUD overlays, dense equations, excessive characters, complex multi-panel comics, decorative clutter, and illegible microtext.
